task: skeptic VALUE+FEASIBILITY of R13NC-2 (public annotation density cannot make generic pruning pay; model-A wording for I-130/I-147/I-312)
reason: The core claim holds on re-check. Metric: adj = max(0, J*(1-0.1*(Npred-Nest)/Nest)), confirmed in metrics.py l.439-449. The per-clip trade-off J*0.1*k/Nest - f*m*e/w, with w and m both proportional to density d, cancels d when the relative enrichment r is fixed. In ncarms_agg.json the 44b6/6bba enrichment ratio across 20 arms is 0.6-1.9 (median ~1.1-1.2). Model B (fixed absolute rate) predicts 5.20/0.79 = 6.6x, so model A is the right description. The numbers check out: model-B thresholds q/r* = 0.67%/0.047 = 14% and 0.55%/0.047 = 12%. Per-embryo absolutes are 0.029*0.79% = 0.023% and 0.049*5.20% = 0.25%. Round 11's 0.16% is r* times the pooled 3.3%. The conclusion is robust to the unknown hidden embryo: r* depends on rho = Npred/Nest (~0.046*rho for interior nodes, ~0.09*rho for leaves), and generic groups at r 0.13-0.44 would need rho ~3-9 to break even. Two overstatements need fixing. (1) 'Embryo-invariant' uses the three closest pairs. comp<=6 is 0.39/0.21 and leaf_p<0.3 is 0.22/0.13 (~1.8-1.9x), and the 44b6 counts are only 5-36 matched nodes. The tilt raises r on the sparse embryo, which makes pruning worse there, so the conclusion is unchanged. (2) In the readmit flip, the 7 TP lost on 44b6 are exactly the model-A expectation (0.16*0.0079*5323 = 6.7), so they are not noise. The flip comes from the FP term: 6bba-scaled FP would be -4.7 against the observed +4, i.e. ~8.7 FP x 2.6e-4 = ~0.0023, which is essentially the whole flip. The lower rho on 44b6 accounts for the rest. Feasibility is trivial: this is curator wording only, with no mechanism, submission, R8 slot, dummy or user OK. It is a closure argument, not a closed line in disguise.
fix: Adopt the finding with two wording changes. (a) Replace 'embryo-invariant' with 'roughly density-free: the 44b6/6bba enrichment ratio is 0.6-1.9 across 20 arms (median ~1.1), while a fixed absolute rate would give 6.6x. The 44b6 counts are small (5-36 matched).' (b) Replace 'FP-edge removal plus noise' with 'the FP-edge term (6bba dFP -44 vs 44b6 +4; ~0.0023 of the 44b6 gap) plus lower rho on 44b6 (0.71 vs 1.02). The 44b6 TP cost equals the model-A expectation.' Also correct the NODES impact line in research/KNOWLEDGE/IDEAS.md (l.61 and l.341) and the I-312 text, which currently say 'node levers flip sign by embryo because annotation density differs'. Wording: 'break-even is relative: r* ~0.03-0.05 (x rho), about 0.02-0.04% absolute on 44b6 and ~0.25% on 6bba; public density sets the noise, not the sign.'
